newsitem.title: USA: US W. Coast crude falls with NYMEX before holiday.
newsitem.headline: US W. Coast crude falls with NYMEX before holiday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude oil prices edged up Monday, reflecting a modest rise in other domestic crude market while spot trade remained subdued, traders said.

No spot buyers of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, the region's benchmark grade, stepped forward, but traders said Atlantic Richfield Co. (ARCO) sold two cargoes on a formula basis, or the monthly average of wire service price quotes.

Traders said ARCO sold the cargoes because they had excess supply in the wake of refinery problems in May. The formula deal allowed them to get rid of the barrels without using discount markets, which oftenlead to a stalemate over price. By using formula basis, oth buyer and seller avoided gambling on whether the discount will changed radically in the coming month, traders said.
With the discount flat, outright prices for ANS crude oil were pulled up by slightly higher NYMEX and WTI cash prices.
Line 63 barrels also gained in line with the NYMEX and cash crude.
Kern River and Wilmington crudes -- California heavy grades -- were unchanged.
Foreign spot buying remained stagnant for August crude while Oriente seen the barrel of choice this month, traders said.
Both U.S Oil and Tosco's Los Angeles and Bay refineries remained at reduced rates of crude oil runs, traders said, due to poor refining margins.
